description: Part-load electrical + thermal efficiency with ambient temperature derating for Stirling engine micro-CHP

unit.name: Generic 1 kW Stirling Engine Micro-CHP (e.g. WhisperGen / Remeha eVita class)
unit.source: Lund, H. et al. (2016). Smart energy and flexibility. Elsevier; Hawkes, A. & Leach, M. (2007). Cost-effective operating strategy for residential micro-CHP. Energy, 32(5), 711-723; Kongtragool, B. & Wongwises, S. (2003). A review of solar-powered Stirling engines. Renew. Sustain. Energy Rev., 7(2), 131-154.

eta_el_rated.note: Stirling electrical efficiency ~10-15% (lower than SOFC, limited by Carnot for T_hot/T_cold)

eta_th_rated.note: High thermal efficiency (total ~92%): Stirling optimised for heat output

PLR_min.note: Stirling engine minimum stable operation PLR

el_plr_a.note: Electrical PLR constant: Stirling has moderate part-load drop

th_plr_a.note: Thermal PLR constant: Stirling heat output relatively constant (burner-modulated)

temp_derating_pct_per_degC.note: Power derating above 25 degC (Stirling T_cold increase reduces Carnot efficiency)
